share.distribution: about 86% of US and Canadian corn acres in 2015, up from about 80% in 2007

evidence.notes: Vendor survey (Pioneer Brand Concentration Survey); respondent base not given. No newer national survey found; USDA NASS publishes row widths for soybean only.

patterns.name: Wide single rows at 36 to 38 in (91 to 97 cm)

share.distribution: about 7% of acres in 2015 and declining

patterns.name: Narrow rows at 20 or 22 in (51 or 56 cm)

share.distribution: 20 in 3.0%, 22 in 2.6% of acres (2012); all rows under 30 in about 6% (2015); highest in Minnesota then South Dakota, under 5% in the central Corn Belt

evidence.notes: Iowa State: 20 in beat 30 in by 8 to 10 bu/a only above about 235 bu/a.

patterns.name: Twin rows 7 to 8 in apart on 30 in centres

evidence.notes: Pair centres at 30 in; the two lines of a pair 18 to 20 cm apart, staggered along the row. In the South also 9.5 in pairs on 40 in beds (snippet).

patterns.notes: At 2 cm or coarser a twin pair reads as one wide row at the 30 in pitch; finer it is two lines at alternating short and long gaps, and the row reader may report the pair spacing as an alternative pitch.

evidence.notes: Vendor and regional guidance, no practice survey; 70 cm canonical in Italy.

patterns.name: Turkey, 70 cm (60 to 80 coastal, 40 to 60 interior second crop)
Brazil Centre-West, 45 to 50 cm (shares the soybean planter)

evidence.notes: 80 to 90 cm historically; trials 45 to 90 cm. Trade and extension text, no survey.

patterns.name: Sub-Saharan Africa, ridges at 75 to 90 cm with planting stations

rowSpacingM.distribution: Malawi, 240 fields measured: means 80 to 92 cm, over 75 cm in 90% of fields; 1 to 4 plants per station, mostly 2

evidence.geography: Malawi; trials in Kenya, Nigeria, Zimbabwe

patterns.notes: Stations of two plants at 21 to 115 cm read as clumps, not as singulated plants: the double rule does not apply.

patterns.name: China, 60 to 65 cm uniform rows (wide-narrow 80 + 40 cm trialled)

evidence.geography: Northeast China 65 cm ridges; Huang-Huai-Hai 60 cm

byPopulation.note: 8 plants/m² in 75 cm rows (KWS UK table gives 15.8 cm)
Brazil safrinha survey mean about 55,000 to 60,000/ha

evidence.notes: In-row spacing = 1 / (plants per ha × row spacing in m), our arithmetic from the sourced populations. Harvest stands run 5 to 10% under the seeding rate (UNL G2216); field emergence 90 to 95% (Purdue AGRY-91-01).

plantsPerHa.distribution: fewer than 10% of fields reach the recommended 53,333/ha

skipShare.distribution: share of spacings over 1.5 × nominal; 15 Nebraska sites, 2001; includes 5 to 10% non-emergence

doubleShare.distribution: share of spacings under 0.5 × nominal; 15 Nebraska sites

spacingSdCm.distribution: Indiana and Ohio 354 fields (1987 to 1996) mean SD about 4.5 in; Wisconsin 127 fields mean 3.3 in (1.9 to 6.8)

evidence.disagreement: Its yield cost is contested: 2.2 to 4.5 bu/a per inch of SD (Purdue, Pioneer) against no effect (Wisconsin, Ontario); the geometry figures agree.

singulation.emergenceNotes: Doubles sit 2.5 to 5 cm apart and read as one blob from above. Late emergers are one to two leaves behind; a one-week gap is about two leaf stages, so an uneven field shows two plant sizes along the row. Late-emerger frequency in commercial fields: not found.

guessRowErrorCm.distribution: measured means 7.4 manual, 5.0 CORS, 5.9 SBAS, 6.7 RTK (Turkey, 24 corn and cotton fields); receiver specs SF1 ±15, SF2 ±5, SF3 ±3, RTK ±2.5 cm (95%, 15 min); up to 23 cm on SF1-class signal

evidence.notes: No North American corn-planter measurement found.

planterGeometry.notes: Within one planter pass the pitch is exact; between passes (every 12, 16 or 24 rows on most farms) the guess row may be off by 5 to 15 cm. The row reader's per-window fits absorb a guess row only when a window does not straddle it.

fieldGeometry.name: Headlands and end rows
fieldGeometry.description: 2 to 4 planter widths planted perpendicular to the field body at each end (farmers report at least 12 rows, 16 for large combines).
fieldGeometry.imageryEffect: Rows change direction by 90 degrees; a window straddling the turn has two plantings and no clean pitch. Edge weeds concentrate here too.

fieldGeometry.name: Point rows
fieldGeometry.description: Short rows where a field edge is not parallel to the planting; without section control 0.1 to 20% of a field may be double-planted.
fieldGeometry.imageryEffect: Overlapping plantings at an angle: crossed rows, doubled plant density, and rows that end abruptly.

fieldGeometry.name: Guess rows between planter passes
fieldGeometry.description: The gap between adjacent passes, 5 to 15 cm off the nominal pitch.
fieldGeometry.imageryEffect: A pitch anomaly every 12, 16 or 24 rows; harmless to a per-window fit, visible as a phase jump between windows.

fieldGeometry.name: Contour and terrace planting
fieldGeometry.description: Rows following contours; Iowa alone has about 506,100 terraces. Share of corn on contours: not found.
fieldGeometry.imageryEffect: Rows curve; per-window direction changes; long windows blur the pitch.

fieldGeometry.name: Centre-pivot fields
fieldGeometry.description: A 160-acre circle in a quarter section leaves about 25 acres of corners; rows usually straight across the circle, circular only under some LEPA systems.
fieldGeometry.imageryEffect: Wheel tracks as concentric arcs; dry corners with different stand or weeds.

fieldGeometry.name: Row direction
fieldGeometry.description: No convention found; usually the field's long axis. Yield trials disagree on east-west versus north-south.
fieldGeometry.imageryEffect: None for the reader, which searches every angle; sun azimuth against row direction decides whether shadows fall into the alley.

share.distribution: 16% of corn acres in 2001, 28% in 2016, 36% in 2021

tillage.residueAppearance: Previous crop's residue lies between and along the rows; after corn, old stalk rows offset about half a row (15 in) from the new rows in corn-on-corn; after soybeans, thin grey stubble with faint drill lines. In bright light the straw is brighter than the soil and forms stripes at the crop's own pitch.

evidence.notes: The residue-pattern description is our inference from the planting geometry, confirmed on one photo (0359, red soil with straw strips); unsourced in the literature.

tillage.residueAppearance: A dark tilled band 20 to 25 cm wide on each row centre, residue between: a stripe pattern at the crop pitch, in phase with the rows.

evidence.notes: ERS folds strip-till into no-till; 7.7% of cropland in 2014 by a trade estimate; 84% of strip-tillers on 30 in rows.

share.distribution: continuous full-width tillage on 55% of corn land in 2016

tillage.residueAppearance: Mostly bare soil; plough or disc furrows may show as faint stripes not at the crop pitch.

gaps: No US row-width survey newer than the 2015 Pioneer vendor survey; USDA NASS publishes measured row widths for soybean only.
Twin-row share rests on vendor statements (under 1%) and a 2009 snippet (under 0.2%).
Europe, Brazil and China spacings come from trial baselines and trade text, not practice surveys; Malawi (240 fields) is the only measured distribution outside the US.
Guess-row error measured on North American corn planters: not found (Turkish and Brazilian measurements and receiver specs stand in).
Headland depth, point-row area and their share of fields: forum and section-control snippets only.
Share of corn on contours and terraces, and of pivot corn planted in circles: not found.
Late-emerger frequency in commercial fields: not found.
Residue appearance by previous crop and tillage: the descriptions are ours; the Purdue residue-cover table could not be fetched.
